The amount of money needed to fund the future of AI is so large that Wall Street has been rewriting the rules to finance it

The money needed to finance AI infrastructure is creating big opportunities for Wall Street. The stakes are getting higher, as political scrutiny could slow projects and drive up costs. Meet seven rising stars finding innovative ways to fund the AI boom.

Financing that buildout is no simple task. It's pushed bankers and investors to develop new financing structures and tap different pools of capital.

The outlook has become more complicated following Democrats' landslide victory in the midterm elections, as many candidates' campaign promises included slowing data center construction and tightening oversight. That scrutiny could potentially delay projects , drive up costs, and make it harder for investors to earn the returns they anticipated.For Diana Liu, a principal at Blue Owl who has spent more than a decade investing in data centers, navigating these challenges is part of the business.

"Development has never been simple," she told Business Insider following the election. "Experience and long-term local relationships matter more than ever, because a data center project only works when the community, the tenant and the developer all want it to."Still, the enormous scale of the AI buildout means there will be plenty of work to do.

"We are still in the early innings, with a long runway ahead," said Maya Venkatraman, a managing director at Morgan Stanley,Both are among Business Insider's 2026 Rising Stars of Wall Street , seven of whom are helping finance the AI infrastructure boom.

Meet the crew bankrolling the technology through multibillion-dollar bond offerings, innovative financing, and investments in the power plants and data centers that will underpin the AI economy.

Cody Kiechle, 33, Bank of America Cody Kiechle grew up milking cows and driving tractors on his family's dairy farm in a small town near the Canadian border in northern New York. Now, he's helping finance the biggest infrastructure buildouts in technology history.The 33-year-old Bank of America managing director has helped execute more than 400 bond offerings that raised over $1 trillion over his career, including more than $200 billion in 2026 alone.He's at the center of an unprecedented borrowing spree as technology giants race to build AI infrastructure. Historically, these companies used relatively little outside financing. But Kiechle recognized a turning point in late 2025, when it became clear that their businesses were becoming far more capital-intensive and would turn to debt."There was a pretty massive shift happening," he said.So far in 2026, nine bond offerings have reached $25 billion or more, compared with a previous full-year record of just two deals that size.Kiechle has led and advised on four of these megadeals. He expects the AI borrowing boom to accelerate into 2027 and believes this period will be remembered as a "seminal moment."Kiechle's recent deals include helping Alphabet raise $32 billion from investors, securing $25 billion apiece for Oracle and Salesforce, and leading SpaceX's first public bond sale, which raised $25 billion. The Oracle deal attracted a record amount of investor orders for a bond offering from a highly rated company, Kiechle said.The complexity of these megadeals can be "stressful at times, super exciting at times," Kiechle said. The Alphabet transaction happened over a couple of days, and he worked across multiple time zones to raise money in US dollars, British pounds, and Swiss francs.After attending Harvard, Kiechle joined Bank of America in 2015. He spent three years in debt capital markets, moved into investment banking, then returned, taking primary responsibility for technology clients in 2024.He credits his rural upbringing with teaching him "work ethic," "comfort with unpredictability," and "an ownership mindset."Now a mentor himself, Kiechle previously oversaw professional development for more than 50 junior bankers. He typically passes along advice he received early in his career: "Be comfortable being uncomfortable." Business Insider USA

Diana Liu, 33, Blue Owl Capital People might think Diana Liu had some foresight when she started working on financing data center deals 12 years ago. But really, she was just starting out in structured finance at Deutsche Bank and found that because data centers didn't fit neatly into traditional real estate or infrastructure portfolios, they created an opportunity to earn "excess returns" relative to the risk.More than a decade later, Liu said the sector still offers outsized returns not because there aren't investors, but because hyperscalers can't stop growing.In her role as a Principal at Blue Owl, she helped develop the novel JV structure behind the financing for Meta's $50 billion Hyperion data center in Louisiana, dubbed Project Beignet. Conversations about the deal began when Liu was still at IPI Partners, the data center specialists that Blue Owl acquired in 2025, and she had been at since 2021.The deal, financed 80% by Blue Owl and 20% by Meta, raised more than $27 billion and pioneered the use of 144A bonds in data-center financing at an unprecedented scale. The approach gave them access to a wider pool of institutional investors without requiring them to register the securities.While some may have criticized the deal for taking some of Meta's AI computing costs off its balance sheet, she said it is "the most public deal ever done in data centers" because of the novel use of public bonds."It's always been a progression of trying to become a mainstream asset class and be recognized and be able to access traditional forms of markets," Liu said. "This was a push towards that, not trying to hide something."The business growth has come from a pretty simple investment thesis: supporting the biggest tech companies, the Princeton grad said. It's "a bet that these really financially healthy companies" will continue to support "diversified users of the internet" alongside AI. Massive AI campuses require underwriting AI monetization because of their size, but the core bet is still on big tech."Still to this day, we're a little bit indifferent as to what their use cases are because we think these are some of the best credits in the world," Liu said. Business Insider USA

Maya Venkatraman, 34, Morgan Stanley Maya Venkatraman is helping create the blueprint for Wall Street's data-center debt boom.Venkatraman, a managing director, played a leading role in structuring a novel $3.2 billion bond for data center developer TeraWulf, with credit support from Google."There wasn't really a playbook that existed," said Venkatraman, Morgan Stanley's US head of transportation and infrastructure leveraged finance. Traditional project financing couldn't meet the industry's enormous capital needs alone, so her team developed the structure last fall, which has since served as a template for a market she said has generated roughly $45 billion in high-yield bond issuance over the past year.Venkatraman also had to educate investors and ratings agencies about the emerging asset class, swapping traditional roadshows for visits to data-center project sites, steel-toed boots and all.The deal was "really defining" for Mumbai-born Venkatraman, who joined Morgan Stanley in 2013 and was promoted to MD in January 2026. She's led the structuring and execution of more than 110 transactions throughout her career.It also wasn't the first time dealing with unconventional financing solutions. p: AI의 미래에 자금을 대는 데 필요한 금액은 너무나 막대하여 월스트리트는 이를 조달하기 위해 규칙을 다시 쓰고 있다.
AI 인프라 자금 조달은 월스트리트에 큰 기회를 창출하고 있다. 정치적 엄격 심사가 프로젝트를 지연시키고 비용을 끌어올릴 수 있어 리스크는 점점 더 커지고 있다. AI 붐에 자금을 대는 혁신적인 방법을 찾아낸 7명의 라이징 스타들을 만나본다.

그러한 인프라 구축에 자금을 조달하는 것은 결코 단순한 작업이 아니다. 이는 은행가들과 투자자들이 새로운 금융 구조를 개발하고 다양한 자본 풀을 활용하도록 만들었다.

중대선거에서 민주당이 압승을 거둔 이후 전망은 더욱 복잡해졌으며, 많은 후보들의 선거 공약에는 데이터 센터 건설 속도 조절과 규제 강화가 포함되어 있었다. 그러한 심사는 잠재적으로 프로젝트를 지연시키고, 비용을 끌어올리며, 투자자들이 예상했던 수익을 달성하기 어렵게 만들 수 있다. 데이터 센터 투자에 10년 이상을 보낸 Blue Owl의 프린시펄인 Diana Liu에게 이러한 난관을 헤쳐나가는 것은 비즈니스의 일부이다.

그는 선거 이후 Business Insider와의 인터뷰에서 "개발이 단순했던 적은 결코 없었다"며, "데이터 센터 프로젝트는 지역사회, 임차인, 그리고 디벨로퍼 모두가 원할 때만 성사되기 때문에 경험과 장기적인 지역 네트워크가 그 어느 때보다 중요하다"고 말했다.그럼에도 불구하고 AI 인프라 구축의 엄청난 규모는 해야 할 일이 여전히 산적해 있음을 의미한다.
Morgan Stanley의 매니징 디렉터인 Maya Venkatraman은 "우리는 여전히 초기 단계에 있으며, 앞으로 나아갈 길이 멀다"고 말했다.두 사람 모두 Business Insider가 선정하는 2026 월스트리트의 라이징 스타 7인에 포함되었으며, 이들은 AI 인프라 붐의 자금 조달을 돕고 있다.
수십억 달러 규모의 채권 발행, 혁신적인 금융 구조, 그리고 AI 경제의 토대가 될 발전소와 데이터 센터에 대한 투자를 통해 이 기술에 자금을 공급하는 주역들을 만나본다.
